messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT NOTICE — High error rate (5xx) and token spike from us-east region detected. Paging SRE rotation. Alert: latency > 2s P95, increased 503s on /v1/generate and emb route.
Megan (SRE): I’m on it. Picking up pager. Looking at the us-east allocator metrics now.
Raj (Runtime): I see concurrent batch size jump and GPU OOM retries in the us-east pool. Suspect a bad rollout to small-quant model variant.
Kai (Eng-Platform): confirming — an automated rollout to model: redwood/large-q4x (variant b) started 10m ago in us-east for canary.
Megan (SRE): copying logs. Running quick query:
```
kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=us-east -o wide
# found 3 pods in CrashLoopBackOff, many with kernel OOM logs
```
Megan (SRE): Impact: ~18% elevated 5xx for customer-facing routes; internal smoke tests failing for long seqs. Est. affected customers: mixed free + some paid endpoints routed to us-east.
Alex (Support): We already have two customer tickets reporting slow completions in the last 7m — noting increased severity.
Raj (Runtime): Immediate mitigation idea: revert canary, and throttle long-sequence requests for the next 30m. Recommend: 1) disable canary rollout 2) apply dynamic rate limit on seq_len>2048 3) reroute new traffic away from us-east to us-west primary.
Kai (Eng-Platform): I can flip routing weights and short-circuit canary. Steps: `dispatchctl set-weight region=us-east weight=0.2` then `dispatchctl set-weight region=us-west weight=0.8`. Also can toggle feature-flag `model_canary_us_east=false`.
Megan (SRE): Proceeding with controlled actions. Notifying customers via status page after mitigation.
Megan (SRE): Action 1 — disabling canary now.
deploy-bot: deploy event: feature-flag model_canary_us_east set to false by Megan — propagation underway.
Raj (Runtime): Action 2 — applying temporary short-seq prioritization and soft brownout for long-running completions. Command I’ll apply:
```
rlctl create --scope=region:us-east --policy=soft_brownout_longseq --max-qps=20 --match="route:/v1/generate & seq_len>2048"
```
Kai (Eng-Platform): Action 3 — ramping traffic away from us-east. Running dispatchctl & verifying session affinity.
Megan (SRE): Observability: P95 improved from 2.1s -> 1.4s within the first 90s after routing change. 5xx rate down by ~60% from peak.
Alex (Support): Noted. Updating customer tickets: "We're routing traffic to healthy region while we investigate; expect improved success rates shortly."
Raj (Runtime): Follow-up: we still see elevated memory pressure on a subset of us-east machines related to KV cache retention for long seqs. Suggest clearing prefix cache for canary group and avoid heavy K/V warm starts.
Megan (SRE): Raj, can you do a cache eviction for the canary model keys?
Raj (Runtime): On it: `cachectl evict --model redwood/large-q4x --scope=us-east --prefix=canary-*` — eviction complete.
Megan (SRE): Deploy-bot logs show canary pods terminating gracefully. CrashLoopBackOff pods are not restarting now.
Kai (Eng-Platform): Traffic-weight now: us-west 85%, us-east 15% (slow ramp-down to avoid breaking sticky sessions).
Megan (SRE): Monitoring customer errors and latency. We should keep the soft brownout in place for 60 minutes and revisit.
Alex (Support): Triage note: two customers on paid dedicated routes were affected briefly; reached out with mitigation summary. No major data loss.
Raj (Runtime): Root cause hypothesis: model variant b has an unexpected KV cache growth pattern for long-seq that caused OOM under certain batch aggregation. Will roll back binary variant and run synthetic load tests.
Megan (SRE): Handoff note — Megan handing to Kai for continued routing stabilization and to Raj for runtime root-cause. On-call rotation: @next-sre please ack.
Kai (Eng-Platform): Acknowledged. I’ll keep weights at 85/15 for 30m and then evaluate. Also enabling auto-fallback policy to a lower-memory quantized variant for sessions that still get errors.
Megan (SRE): Postmortem template: collect timeline, canary config, memory traces, cache growth graphs, customer impact (tickets & CS outreach). I'll create the incident doc in the incidents tracker.
Alex (Support): I'll follow up with affected customers with the detailed timeline once we have the rollback confirmation.
Megan (SRE): Closing pager: system metrics stabilized and 5xx near baseline. Keeping the thread open for the postmortem artifacts. :white_check_mark:
Kai (Eng-Platform): note — we should add a guard to block large-seq canaries in the future or require gradual concurrency ramp. Filing a follow-up PR idea in platform backlog.
Raj (Runtime): I’ll schedule the deeper repro run on a staging cluster with long-seq workload.
Megan (SRE): Thanks team. Leaving the brownout window until 15:25 UTC and then we'll restore normal weights if metrics are green.
deploy-bot: scheduled action — revert brownout at 15:25 UTC unless cancelled.
Megan (SRE): last check: 5xx rate = baseline + 1.3% — marking incident as mitigated.
Kai (Eng-Platform): Acknowledged. Post-incident: add canary kill-switch and a seq_len safety limit to the rollout policy.
Alex (Support): Adding customer note to status page: short summary + link to incident doc when ready.
Megan (SRE): thread closed for active mitigation; will reopen for postmortem edits. Thanks."
